newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes higher on exporter deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes higher on exporter deals.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Monday due to exporter negotiations carried foward from the weekend and sharply falling trade deficit in May, dealers said.
Customs-cleared trade deficit narrowed sharply to $686 million in May from a $1.44 billion shortfall a year earlier.
The won finished at 890.90, comparing with Friday's close of 891.00. After opening at 891.00, it rose to 890.00 on exporter deals transferred from the weekend.
Dealers said the won was trapped in a narrow range as banks remained uncertain over a possibility of central bank intervention.
"The market is unlikely to escape from the current narrow range trading," said a foreign bank dealer.
A local bank dealer forecast the won/dollar would move in a 890.50-893.00 range for the time being.
Trading volume was estimated at $900 million. Tuesday's mid-rate was expected to be fixed at 891.20 against 891.80 today.
